Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: SeyID provides full digital authentication capability. The platform supports: passwordless QR code login, OTP (one-time password) authentication, OpenID Connect/OAuth integration, PKI-based digital signatures, and eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer). WISeKey's announcement confirms 'WISeID supports seamless online KYC onboarding, one-time password (OTP) authentication, and innovative hands-free secure login through QR-codes'. DICT website lists 'Secure Login' and 'OTP Generator' among SeyID functions.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: SeyID is the mandatory authentication mechanism for the monServis government services portal (monservis.gov.sc). The Seychelles Licensing Authority's online services page states: 'all users must register for the new SeyID to be able to access monServis and use SLA online services.' DICT confirms SeyID 'provides convenience and security for accessing government services online.' Services accessible include business licenses, vehicle licenses, and other government transactions.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 grants data subjects the right to access, request correction or deletion of their data, block access, and oppose usage for specific purposes (Section 19). The SeyID platform allows users to view their own NIN, date of birth, and ID details in the virtual card. The DPA also grants rights to data portability and rectification. Citizens can request copies of their civil registration records through CertExpress.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: SeyID explicitly includes eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) as a core function. The SeyID portal states 'eKYC (Electronic Know Your Customer) is the remote, paperless process that minimises the costs and traditional bureaucracy necessary in KYC processes.' The QR code on the virtual ID enables bank account opening verification. WISeKey's announcement confirms SeyID supports KYC for banking services. The system is used by financial institutions for customer onboarding.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Seychelles has general judicial oversight through its courts, and the Data Protection Act 2023 provides rights of appeal against enforcement notices to the Commission (Section 13). The Constitution (Article 20) recognises the right to privacy. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms (such as dedicated ID ombudsman, ID appeals tribunal, or constitutional court review of ID-specific issues) have been identified in available sources.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Seychelles has a fully integrated CRVS-identity system. The National Population Database (established 1988) is fed directly from the Civil Status Division's civil registration records and is updated daily. The NIN assigned via NPD is derived from civil registration. The Civil Status Act requires registration of all births, marriages, and deaths. The SeyID system links to the NIN from the NPD/Civil Status Department. CertExpress (launched 2024) digitally delivers birth, marriage, and death certificates linked to the NIN and SeyID digital wallet.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 establishes partial data sharing rules: it sets consent requirements, data minimisation principles, purpose limitation, and cross-border transfer safeguards (Seychelles is the first African country to recognise the CBPR mechanism). The SeyID eKYC explicitly requires customer approval before sending identity data to service providers. However, a comprehensive published data-sharing framework specifically for the identity system has not been identified; the DPA's 18-month transition period runs until mid-2025.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: As of 2024, Seychelles does not have a dedicated stand-alone digital identity law. The SeyID system is implemented under broader ICT and civil status legislation. The Data Protection Act 2023 covers data handling aspects. The Civil Status Act regulates NIN. The 2022 budget announced plans for frameworks to develop the digital economy but a specific digital ID regulation has not been identified in available sources.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Seychelles enacted the Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023), signed by President Ramkalawan on 19 December 2023 and published on 22 December 2023. It replaces the Data Protection Act 2003 which was never implemented in practice. The 2023 Act aligns with GDPR principles, covers rights of data subjects, creates enforcement mechanisms including fines, mandates data protection impact assessments for high-risk activities, and provides for cross-border data transfer safeguards.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2023 designates the Information Commission (established under the Access to Information Act) as the competent authority to enforce data protection law. The Commission has powers to conduct investigations, audits, issue enforcement notices, impose fines up to SCR 200,000, and order suspension of data flows. This constitutes an operational data protection authority with oversight of digital identity data.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The physical National Identity Card is mandatory for all Seychellois residents and constitutes legal proof of identity for official transactions per the Civil Status Department. The SeyID virtual ID includes a QR code for secure third-party verification and is legally accepted: as of September 2024, work permit holders must use the virtual ID system, replacing physical card issuance. The digital driving license via SeyID is also legally accepted. The 2022 budget speech confirmed the electronic ID system has legal operational status.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Seychelles has a well-established legal framework for identity. The Civil Status Act governs civil registration and identity management (originally 1893, updated to 2022). The National Identity Number system has been compulsory by law since 1995. The Data Protection Act 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) enacted December 2023 provides a comprehensive legal framework covering digital data processing, privacy rights, and oversight. The Minister for Finance announced in November 2022 budget that the digital ID system is legally operational.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The SeyID platform was developed and is maintained by WISeKey (a Swiss company), representing significant foreign vendor involvement. However, DICT (Department of Information and Communication Technology) was noted by the World Bank (2020) as having 'a solid foundation' of in-house technical capacity, and systems deployed in government ministries have often been built in-house. Local company Victoria Computer Services (VCS) handles level 1 and 2 technical interventions for the biometric passport system. The arrangement reflects partial in-country capability alongside WISeKey's platform ownership.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance plays a partial oversight role. The 2022 budget speech by Finance Minister Naadir Hassan explicitly referred to the SeyID system as 'key to the Digital Economy Agenda', allocated R145.1 million in 2023 for ICT projects, and announced priorities for SeyID platform integration. The World Bank Digital Government report recommended giving DICT 'a Ministry of Finance backed power to veto spending on technology projects' — suggesting this power was not yet fully formalised. Finance oversees budgetary allocations but full formal oversight mechanism is not confirmed.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Seychelles collects both facial and fingerprint biometrics. The biometric passport introduced in November 2022 includes an electronic chip with facial recognition and fingerprint data. The SeyID eKYC process uses facial video selfie for verification. The National Population Database contains biographic and photographic data. Biometric passports are produced by IN Groupe with full biometric collection at enrollment stations.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The National Population Database (NPD) was established digitally in 1988 and is updated daily from civil status registrations. The NIN (National Identity Number) system has been compulsory since 1995. The SeyID platform operates on a fully digital cloud-based infrastructure. The World Bank's Digital Government report (2020) notes that 'there is a considerable amount of other government data that is already digitised' and characterises Seychelles as having a comprehensive digital identity database.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Seychelles operates a fully deployed nationwide digital ID ecosystem comprising: (1) a long-standing compulsory physical National Identity Card (NIC) underpinned by the National Population Database (NPD) introduced in 1988; and (2) the SeyID digital identity platform, launched November 2022 and built on WISeKey's WISeID, which was formally delivered and operational by April 2024. The SeyID system is web- and app-based, integrated with eGovernment services (monServis portal), licensing authority, and private sector including banking. It is mandatory for work permit holders as of September 2024.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The SeyID platform is explicitly designed for interoperability: it integrates with the Department of Immigration and Civil Status (NIN/ID database), the Seychelles Licensing Authority, and the monServis eGovernment portal. The QR code on virtual IDs enables third-party verification including bank account opening. The system uses OpenID Connect/OAuth standards enabling integration with corporate applications. DICT is the coordinator of government-wide digital services integration.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: SeyID is accepted but not mandatory for banking. The UK GOV guidance on living in Seychelles states banks require 'a valid identification document (e.g., passport or national identity card)' to open accounts. The SeyID QR code enables 'bank account opening' verification. The SeyID platform was in 'final integration phases with eGovernment and private enterprises, including banking services' at launch (2022). WISeKey's announcement confirms SeyID supports KYC for eBanking. Physical NIC/passport remain accepted alternatives.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The National Identity Card is free of charge on first issuance for Seychellois nationals per the ICS FAQ: 'The I.D card is free of charge on first issuance.' A replacement for lost card costs SCR 150. The SeyID digital platform is also free to access and register. Wikipedia notes a cost of SR50 for Seychelles NIC, but the official ICS source states first issuance is free. The SeyID app and web registration do not charge fees.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Seychelles has some regional cross-border recognition. The biometric passport (compliant with ICAO 9303 standards, 8th edition) enables visa-free travel to 152 countries (ranked No.1 in Africa per Henley Passport Index). SeyID supports tourist digital IDs for visitors. The AU Interoperability Framework for Digital ID (which Seychelles as an AU member state participates in) aims to enable continental ID interoperability but formal bilateral ID interoperability agreements have not been confirmed as fully operational.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The physical NIC is compulsory for all Seychellois citizens (age not explicitly restricted in ICS source, suggesting from birth/registration). Foreign nationals below age 16 receive a physical card with no photo. For SeyID digital ID, eligibility is explicitly 'over 15 years old'. Wikipedia notes Seychelles NIC is 'Compulsory for all Seychelles citizens'. The ICS states residents must hold a valid NIC. Enrollment eligibility for the digital component begins at 16 (fitting the 10-17 bracket).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The physical National Identity Card is mandatory for all Seychellois residents per the ICS website: 'It is mandatory for all residents of Seychelles to hold a valid National Identity Card.' Foreign nationals with work permits above 16 are also required to enroll. As of September 2024, SeyID (virtual ID) is mandatory for new work permit holders. The NIN has been compulsory by law since June 1995. This constitutes mandatory enrollment for all.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: SeyID was specifically integrated with eHealth as part of its launch scope. The 2022 launch announcement lists 'eHealth' as one of three integration domains alongside eGovernment and eTourism. The 2023 budget speech references a health information system coming into operation by end 2022. The health system uses NIN as a patient identifier. However, no source confirms healthcare access is formally mandatory with ID; it is accepted for accessing health services.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: All categories of non-nationals residing in Seychelles are eligible for identity credentials. Foreign workers and their dependents above age 16 receive a National Identity Number and are directed to register for the virtual SeyID. Foreign nationals below 16 receive a physical card with no photo. The ICS website explicitly states foreign nationals are required to hold an NIC for the duration of their permit. Additionally, SeyID enables tourists to create a digital tourist ID for accessing local digital services.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: The National Identity Card is compulsory for all Seychellois citizens and all resident foreign nationals (above age 16). The World Bank Digital Government report (2020) notes that 'Seychelles has a comprehensive identity database, with cards that are widely used and widely held' and describes it as a key national asset. The ICS website confirms it is mandatory for all residents. Given Seychelles' small population (~100,000) and the long-standing compulsory NIN system since 1995, coverage is assessed as exceeding 89%.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No publicly available evidence of formal, independent security audits or penetration testing of the SeyID or NIC systems has been found. The World Bank Digital Government report (2020) explicitly flagged as a threat: 'Security. All ICT systems are at risk of compromising incidents... This threat is exacerbated by a lack of security investment, especially in regular penetration testing.' WISeKey uses its Swiss Root of Trust (OE/WISeKey) and blockchain technologies for security, but independent third-party security review publication has not been identified.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration requiring national ID is mandatory in Seychelles. A December 2020 Seychelles Nation article describes stricter SIM registration regulations: carriers must verify and record customer personally identifiable information prior to SIM activation; unregistered SIMs were deactivated by January 2021. PikaSim (2026) confirms 'Seychelles requires national ID or passport registration for SIM cards. Carriers must maintain customer identification records under telecommunications regulations.' National ID or passport is the required document.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is accepted (and in practice required) for social protection services in Seychelles. The Agency for Social Protection administers pensions, social welfare, disability benefits. The World Bank PforR social protection program (2021) notes the NIN/ID system is used across social programs. While formal mandatory use is not explicitly confirmed in a single decree, the ID is the standard identification document for accessing government services. No specific social services mandate excluding alternative ID has been identified.
